solution_sources.worked_solution:
The complex number shown in the Argand diagram can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =x+\text{i}y \\  & =4+3\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

To write it in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the first quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{3}{4}) \\  & ≈0.644.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=5$ and $\theta =0.644$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=5\,{\text{e}}^{0.644\,\text{i}}.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
The complex number shown in the Argand diagram can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =x+\text{i}y \\  & =-1+\sqrt{3}\,\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

To write it in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{(\sqrt{3})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the second quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (-\sqrt{3})| \\  & =\pi -\frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=2$ and $\theta =\frac{2\pi }{3}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=2\,{\text{e}}^{2\pi \text{i}/3}.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
The complex number shown in the Argand diagram can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =x+\text{i}y \\  & =\sqrt{3}+\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

To write it in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(\sqrt{3})}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the first quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=2$ and $\theta =\frac{\pi }{6}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=2\,{\text{e}}^{\pi \text{i}/6}.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
The complex number shown in the Argand diagram can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =x+\text{i}y \\  & =2-3\,\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

To write it in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-3)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (-\frac{3}{2})| \\  & ≈5.3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{13}$ and $\theta =5.3$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=\sqrt{13}\,{\text{e}}^{5.3\,\text{i}}.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
The complex number shown in the Argand diagram can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =x+\text{i}y \\  & =1+3\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

To write it in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the first quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan} (3) \\  & ≈1.249.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{10}$ and $\theta =1.249$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=\sqrt{10}\,{\text{e}}^{1.249\,\text{i}}.
$$

The complex number shown in the Argand diagram can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =x+\text{i}y \\  & =3-\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

To write it in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (-\frac{1}{3})| \\  & ≈5.961.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{10}$ and $\theta =5.961$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=\sqrt{10}\,{\text{e}}^{5.961\,\text{i}}.

solution_sources.worked_solution:
The complex number shown in the Argand diagram can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =x+\text{i}y \\  & =2+2\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

To write it in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the first quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan} (1) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=2\sqrt{2}$ and $\theta =\frac{\pi }{4}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=2\sqrt{2}\,{\text{e}}^{\pi \text{i}/4}.
$$

The complex number shown in the Argand diagram can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =x+\text{i}y \\  & =-\sqrt{3}-\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

To write it in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(-\sqrt{3})}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the third quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{-1}{-\sqrt{3}})| \\  & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}})| \\  & =\pi +\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\frac{7\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=2$ and $\theta =\frac{7\pi }{6}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=2\,{\text{e}}^{7\pi \text{i}/6}.
$$

The complex number shown in the Argand diagram can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =x+\text{i}y \\  & =-3+3\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

To write it in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{18} \\  & =3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z$ lies in the second quadrant of the complex plane, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (-1)| \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=3\sqrt{2}$ and $\theta =\frac{3\pi }{4}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=3\sqrt{2}\,{\text{e}}^{3\pi \text{i}/4}.
$$

The complex number shown in the Argand diagram can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =x+\text{i}y \\  & =-4-2\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

To write it in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{20} \\  & =2\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the third quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{-2}{-4})| \\  & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{1}{2})| \\  & ≈\pi +0.463\,64… \\  & ≈3.605.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=2\sqrt{5}$ and $\theta =3.605$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=2\sqrt{5}\,{\text{e}}^{3.605\,\text{i}}\,.
$$

The complex number shown in the Argand diagram can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =x+\text{i}y \\  & =-4+\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

To write it in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{17}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z$ lies in the second quadrant of the complex plane, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (-\frac{1}{4})| \\  & ≈2.897.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{17}$ and $\theta =2.897$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=\sqrt{17}\,{\text{e}}^{2.897\,\text{i}}.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
The complex number shown in the Argand diagram can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =x+\text{i}y \\  & =-2+3\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

To write it in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z$ lies in the second quadrant of the complex plane, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (-\frac{3}{2})| \\  & ≈2.159.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{13}$ and $\theta =2.159$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=\sqrt{13}\,{\text{e}}^{2.159\,\text{i}}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{2}{3}) \\  & ≈0.588.\end{aligned}

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{13}$ and $\theta =0.588$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
The complex number shown in the Argand diagram can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =x+\text{i}y \\  & =3+3\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

To write it in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the first quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan} (1) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=3\sqrt{2}$ and $\theta =\frac{\pi }{4}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=3\sqrt{2}\,{\text{e}}^{\pi \text{i}/4}.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
The complex number shown in the Argand diagram can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =x+\text{i}y \\  & =-4-4\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

To write it in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =4\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the third quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{-4}{-4})| \\  & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan} (1)| \\  & =\pi +\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=4\sqrt{2}$ and $\theta =\frac{5\pi }{4}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=4\sqrt{2}\,{\text{e}}^{5\pi \text{i}/4}.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z$ lies in the second quadrant of the complex plane, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{2}{-1})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (-2)| \\  & ≈2.034.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{5}$ and $\theta =2.034$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=\sqrt{5}\,{\text{e}}^{2.034\,\text{i}}\,.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{(1)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the second quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (-1)| \\  & =\pi -\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{2}$ and $\theta =\frac{3\pi }{4}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=\sqrt{2}\,{\text{e}}^{3\pi \text{i}/4}.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
To write $z$ in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z$ lies in the third quadrant of the complex plane, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{-1}{-3})| \\  & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{1}{3})| \\  & ≈3.463.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{10}$ and $\theta =3.463$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=\sqrt{10}\,{\text{e}}^{3.463\,\text{i}}.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+(-3)^{2}} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the third quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{3}{4})| \\  & ≈\pi +0.643\,50… \\  & ≈3.785.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=5$ and $\theta =3.785$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=5\,{\text{e}}^{3.785\,\text{i}}\,.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
To write $z$ in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =2\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z$ lies in the second quadrant of the complex plane, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (-\frac{1}{2})| \\  & ≈2.678.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=2\sqrt{5}$ and $\theta =2.678$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=2\sqrt{5}\,{\text{e}}^{2.678\,\text{i}}.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+(-3)^{2}} \\  & =3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the third quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{-3}{-3})| \\  & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan} (1)| \\  & =\pi +\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=3\sqrt{2}$ and $\theta =\frac{5\pi }{4}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=3\sqrt{2}\,{\text{e}}^{5\pi \text{i}/4}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (-3)| \\  & ≈1.893.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=2\sqrt{10}$ and $\theta =1.893$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=2\sqrt{10}\,{\text{e}}^{1.893\,\text{i}}.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{(-\sqrt{3})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{12} \\  & =2\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =2\pi -\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})| \\  & =2\pi -\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\frac{11\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=2\sqrt{3}$ and $\theta =\frac{11\pi }{6}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=2\sqrt{3}\,{\text{e}}^{11\pi \text{i}/6}.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(-\sqrt{3})}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the third quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{-1}{-\sqrt{3}})| \\  & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}})| \\  & =\pi +\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\frac{7\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=2$ and $\theta =\frac{7\pi }{6}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=2\,{\text{e}}^{7\pi \text{i}/6}.
$$

To write our complex number in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{(2\sqrt{3})}^{2}} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the second quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (-\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{2})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (-\sqrt{3})| \\  & =\pi -\frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=4$ and $\theta =\frac{2\pi }{3}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=4\,{\text{e}}^{2\pi \text{i}/3}.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
To write $z$ in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z$ lies in the first quadrant of the complex plane, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{2}{1}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan} (2) \\  & ≈1.107.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{5}$ and $\theta =1.107$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=\sqrt{5}\,{\text{e}}^{1.107\,\text{i}}.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{5}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{26}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{-1}{5})| \\  & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (-\frac{1}{5})| \\  & ≈2\pi -0.197\,39… \\  & ≈6.086.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{26}$ and $\theta =6.086$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=\sqrt{26}\,{\text{e}}^{6.086\,\text{i}}.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
To write $z$ in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(3\sqrt{3})^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36}=6\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z$ lies in the first quadrant of the complex plane, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{3}{3\sqrt{3}}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=6$ and $\theta =\frac{\pi }{6}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=6\,{\text{e}}^{\pi \text{i}/6}.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-\sqrt{3})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4}=2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (-\sqrt{3})| \\  & =2\pi -\frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{3}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=2$ and $\theta =\frac{5\pi }{3}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=2\,{\text{e}}^{5\pi \text{i}/3}.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
To write $z$ in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant of the complex plane, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{-2}{3})| \\  & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (-\frac{2}{3})| \\  & ≈5.695.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{13}$ and $\theta =5.695$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=\sqrt{13}\,{\text{e}}^{5.695\,\text{i}}.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(\sqrt{3})}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{12} \\  & =2\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z$ lies in the first quadrant of the complex plane, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan} (\sqrt{3}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=2\sqrt{3}$ and $\theta =\frac{\pi }{3}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=2\sqrt{3}\,{\text{e}}^{\pi \text{i}/3}.
$$

solution_sources.worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{8}=2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{-2}{2})| \\  & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan} (-1)| \\  & =2\pi -\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{7\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=2\sqrt{2}$ and $\theta =\frac{7\pi }{4}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=2\sqrt{2}\,{\text{e}}^{7\pi \text{i}/4}.
$$

prompt_sources.name: Example: Writing a Complex Number in Exponential Form
prompt_sources.problem: Write the complex number $z=4+4\textrm{i}$ in exponential form.
prompt_sources.worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z = r\textrm{e}^{\textrm{i}\theta},$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta = \arg(z),$ we first calculate $r\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =4\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z$ lies in the first quadrant of the complex plane, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg} (z) & =\operatorname{arctan} (\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan} (1) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=4\sqrt{2}$ and $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ into $z=re^{\textrm{i}\theta},$ we get

$$
z = 4\sqrt{2}\,\textrm{e}^{\pi\textrm{i}/4}.
$$
